NO BLOCKERS

CANDIDATE_SHA256: 430c8b636870c5df85993a2a35e38227824f0b7f6c52dbc13f1f8ee40a25e0d3

I reviewed `artifacts/editorial/release-candidates/things-to-do/free-burnaby-park-events-this-week.mdx` at commit a6a448a. Note: no shell tool is available in this session, so I could not recompute the hash myself; the review is of the exact file at the canonical release-candidate path referenced by the stated SHA.

**Factual support and source use.** Every substantive claim in the body traces to the source capture recorded in `artifacts/editorial/research/2026-07-19-evening-transit-burnaby-candidates.json` (captured 2026-07-19T17:08, live City of Burnaby pages): Summer Stages dates (July 14–August 27, 2026), location (Confederation Park, 250 Willingdon Ave, by the spray park), showtimes (11 a.m., 12:15 p.m., 2:30 p.m.; Thursday Family Nights 5:30–8:30 p.m.), free framing, art sessions and lawn games, and the rain-or-shine/extreme-weather caveat. The performer summary (puppet theatre, storytelling, ventriloquism, Balkan folk, Celtic music, Morris dancing, juggling) maps one-to-one to the captured July 21–23 listings. Jim Lorimer details (Wed July 22, 1–2 p.m., 2338 Gilmore Ave, ribbon-cutting at 1 p.m., ice cream while supplies last, play tower/slide/swings/spinners/toddler area, no onsite parking, SkyTrain to Gilmore Station) all match the capture. Attribution is properly hedged throughout ("The City of Burnaby says," "Burnaby lists"). I found no unsupported claims.

**Date arithmetic.** July 21, 22, and 23, 2026 are in fact Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday, so the day-of-week claims and the subtitle's "Wednesday afternoon" are correct, and "this week" is accurate for a Sunday July 19 publish.

**Title/meta fit and structure.** Title, subtitle, description, and readerImpact accurately describe the content; no overclaiming. Structure is clean: timing up front, one section per event, a "How to choose" section, and a Sources list whose three URLs match the research artifact. The events-calendar source is not load-bearing but is harmless.

**Image and frontmatter integrity.** `/images/editorial/2026/07/burnaby-summer-stages-jim-lorimer.png` exists in `public/`, and I viewed it: a park performance scene with spray park and playground, matching the alt text; no garbled text, logos, or identifiable-person issues. Attribution discloses it as a generated editorial image, consistent with the published VSO article's precedent. Frontmatter fields match the pre-promotion schema used by the two published things-to-do articles (review/promotion fields are added at promotion, so their absence is correct).

**Risk and duplication.** Low-risk civic-utility content from primary government sources; no legal or reputational exposure identified. The duplicate check in the research artifact holds — the two existing things-to-do articles cover different Deer Lake Park events.

Two non-blocking nits, at your discretion: the sentence "The transportation note is the reader job" (line 44) is internal-jargon phrasing that may read oddly to the public; and the photorealistic style of the generated hero image could be mistaken for an actual event photo, though the attribution field discloses it.
